title: Crankshaft Position Sensor Fault
shortDescription: No signal from crankshaft position sensor during cranking.
fullDescription:
Yamaha YFI (Yamaha Fuel Injection) error 12 indicates ECU received no reliable pulses from crank sensor. Engine will not start.

Causes include damaged sensor, metallic debris on tip, or broken wiring. MT-07/R1 owners occasionally see this after track use.

fixSteps.title: Remove and clean
fixSteps.instruction: Pull crank sensor, wipe iron debris off tip.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install OEM, torque 10 Nm, clear code.

whenToCallPro: If flywheel tone ring is damaged.
videoSearchQuery: Yamaha motorcycle Er-12 crank sensor fix

title: Intake Air Pressure Sensor Open/Short
shortDescription: IAP sensor (MAP) signal out of range open or shorted.
fullDescription:
Error 13 means IAP voltage stuck high or low. Similar to P0107/P0108 on cars.

Yamaha mounts IAP atop airbox or throttle bodies. Check hose and connector first.

fixSteps.title: Inspect hose
fixSteps.instruction: Secure IAP vacuum hose to throttle body.

videoSearchQuery: Yamaha motorcycle Er-13 IAP sensor fix

title: IAP Sensor Hose Fault
shortDescription: Intake air pressure hose blocked or detached.
fullDescription:
Error 14 specifically flags a plausibility issue on the IAP hose — pressure doesn't change with throttle inputs.

Hose may be kinked, blocked by debris or oil, or detached inside the airbox.

fixSteps.title: Inspect hose path
fixSteps.instruction: Route hose without kinks; replace if cracked.

fixSteps.title: Clear port
fixSteps.instruction: Blow through throttle body vacuum nipple.

videoSearchQuery: Yamaha motorcycle Er-14 IAP hose fix

faq.a: Yes — 13 is circuit, 14 is hose plausibility.

title: TPS Open/Short
shortDescription: Throttle Position Sensor circuit open or shorted.
fullDescription:
Error 15 indicates TPS output out of range. Bike enters safe mode with reduced power on ride-by-wire models.

Often caused by worn wiper track or damaged connector.

fixSteps.title: Diagnostic mode
fixSteps.instruction: Use YDS or diagnostic dongle to view live TPS data.

fixSteps.title: Replace TPS
fixSteps.instruction: On ride-by-wire, replace throttle body assembly.

faq.a: Only after fault repair and ECU reset.

title: Speed Sensor Stuck
fullDescription:
Error 16 reports no VSS pulses. Speedo reads zero and traction control/cruise disable.

Front sprocket area sensors on sport models; rear wheel sensors on ABS bikes.
videoSearchQuery: Yamaha motorcycle Er-16 speed sensor fix

faq.a: Yes, but without TC and cruise.

title: Intake Air Temp Sensor Fault
fullDescription:
Error 17 indicates IAT sensor failure. ECU uses default 25C, running slightly rich.

Inexpensive fix — sensor screws into airbox.
videoSearchQuery: Yamaha motorcycle Er-17 IAT sensor fix

title: Engine Coolant Temp Sensor Fault
fullDescription:
Error 18 is the coolant temp sensor variant. On liquid-cooled bikes ECU defaults to 80C but fan logic is disabled; risk of overheating.

Address soon on sport bikes in traffic.

fixSteps.title: Replace
fixSteps.instruction: Drain small coolant, swap sensor, refill and burp.

whenToCallPro: If full cooling system bleed required.
videoSearchQuery: Yamaha motorcycle Er-18 ECT sensor fix

faq.a: Avoid — no fan control means overheat risk.

title: O2 Sensor Fault
fullDescription:
Error 19 reports O2 sensor issues — aged element, leak nearby, or wiring.

Aftermarket exhausts often trigger this on Yamaha.

fixSteps.title: Fix exhaust
fixSteps.instruction: Repair leaks and ensure bung is present.

whenToCallPro: If ECU mapping needed after exhaust swap.
videoSearchQuery: Yamaha motorcycle Er-19 O2 sensor fix

faq.a: O2 eliminators exist but affect emissions compliance.

title: Sidestand Switch Fault
shortDescription: Sidestand switch circuit open or shorted.
fullDescription:
Error 21 means sidestand switch reads implausible state. ECU may prevent start or cut engine in gear.

Common from water/dirt in switch or bent mounting.

fixSteps.title: Clean switch
fixSteps.instruction: Spray contact cleaner and cycle stand multiple times.

videoSearchQuery: Yamaha motorcycle Er-21 sidestand switch fix

title: Cam Position Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Lean angle / cam sensor signal missing.
fullDescription:
Error 22 refers to lean/cam sensor depending on model year. If cam, timing sync is lost and engine may not start.

Check sensor tip and wiring.
videoSearchQuery: Yamaha motorcycle Er-22 cam sensor fix

faq.a: ECU reverts to crank-only timing; reduced performance.

title: Injector Fault
shortDescription: Injector circuit open or shorted on any cylinder.
fullDescription:
Error 23 indicates ECU detected injector coil issue. May affect single cylinder — bike will run rough on remaining cylinders.

Check connectors first as they are common failure points on Yamaha triples and inline fours.

fixSteps.title: Swap to test
fixSteps.instruction: Move suspect injector to known-good port.

faq.a: No — circuit fault needs mechanical repair.

title: Fall/Tip Detector Tripped
shortDescription: Bank angle sensor registered fall event.
fullDescription:
Error 30 sets when lean angle exceeds threshold. ECU cuts fuel and spark as safety measure.

Resets by cycling ignition if bike is upright.

fixSteps.title: Inspect mount
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure sensor is upright and tightly secured.

videoSearchQuery: Yamaha motorcycle Er-30 tip over sensor fix

faq.a: Yes — prevents fuel pumping with bike down.

title: Lean Angle Sensor Circuit
fullDescription:
Error 41 indicates circuit fault not a trip event. Sensor may be unplugged or failed internally.

Small 3-pin sensor mounted near ECU.
videoSearchQuery: Yamaha motorcycle Er-41 lean angle circuit fix

faq.q: How is this different from Er-30?
faq.a: Er-30 is trip event; Er-41 is circuit fault.

title: ECU Internal Fault
fullDescription:
Error 50 reports ECU CPU or memory fault. Dealer-level diagnosis required.

Frequent cause: water intrusion or severe voltage spike during jump start.

fixSteps.title: Inspect ECU
fixSteps.instruction: Check for moisture inside ECU case.

videoSearchQuery: Yamaha motorcycle Er-50 ECU fault fix

faq.a: Possible on older bikes; new models require OEM.

title: EEPROM Memory Fault
fullDescription:
Error 79 specifically highlights EEPROM defect — similar to Er-50 but narrower.

Occasionally clears after battery reset, but recurring faults need ECU replacement.

faq.a: Usually after electrical surge or aged ECU.
